author.continuation:
C020: a new chapter, sec:p15-w02b-p15-001-poisson-geometric, now has body and annex text, written from Durrett's author version dated 11 January 2019. I opened Examples 1.6.13 and 1.6.14 (book pp. 34-35, PDF pp. 42-43) and Example A.5.6 (pp. 472-473) in this session. The chapter contains:
- all Poisson factorial moments, giving mean lambda and variance lambda;
- all geometric factorial moments r! q^(r-1)/p^r, giving EN = 1/p, EN(N-1) = 2(1-p)/p^2 and var N = (1-p)/p^2;
- a proof that the index of the first occurrence among independent events of probability p has the geometric law;
- a series lemma (discrete expectation as a series, and the negative-binomial series proved without differentiation);
- a method entry, a worked example (Poisson lambda=2 with E X^3 = 22; fair-coin waiting time) and a limits entry (values that are not nonnegative integers, an infinite mean, p=0).
The annex proves every result.

The geometric moments of order 3 and higher go beyond Durrett, who states only orders 1 and 2. The reader text marks them as an extension.

author.continuation:
I wrote new material for the two assigned gaps. Both use Durrett's author version dated 11 January 2019. I read printed pp. 466-469 of the held PDF, and also read printed p. 468 (PDF page 476) as a page image.

C006: the new results are thm:p15-w02b-p15-005-hahn-partitions and thm:p15-w02b-p15-005-density-hahn, with full annex proofs.
- A pair is a Hahn partition exactly when it differs from a given one by a signed-null set.
- The partition is unique exactly when the empty set is the only signed-null set.
- All Hahn partitions give the same Jordan components.
- The source's variant from p. 468 is included: {f>0} ⊆ A ⊆ {f>=0} almost everywhere, with the source's meaning of almost-everywhere inclusion.
- The witness is f = 2x-1 on [0,1], which has three distinct Hahn positive sets: (1/2,1], [1/2,1] and (1/2,1] ∪ C. The last contains the point 0, where f is negative.

C009: the new result is thm:p15-w02b-p15-005-stieltjes-excess, with a full annex proof.
- Any representing pair of Stieltjes measures equals the Jordan components plus one common finite measure rho.
- The pair equals the Jordan components exactly when rho = 0. This holds exactly when the two measures are mutually singular, and exactly when F(inf)+G(inf) equals the total variation |alpha|(R).
- Every finite rho added to both Jordan components gives another representing pair.
- Witnesses: F=G=1_[0,inf), and the 2x-versus-x pair.

Other new content: a procedure (method), a worked example (F=x^2, G=x for the density 2x-1, where rho(R)=3/4) and a limits warning.

gaps: MP-0: Supply the general likelihood-estimation method with a complete consistency/efficiency/regularity presentation. This needs a stated general theorem, with written proof, giving existence and consistency of the maximum-likelihood estimator under explicit identification, compactness/continuity (or concavity) and domination conditions. It also needs an asymptotic normality/efficiency theorem with explicit differentiability, information, localization and remainder conditions, plus the matching multiparameter information statement. At present fisher-estimation-and-regularity.tex gives only finite-family score/information identities (lines 190-242) and exact binomial and Cauchy-median consistency. Lines 16-18 and 231-242 explicitly disclaim any general asymptotic MLE theorem.

ED26-METHOD-likelihood-estimation-C03: Reconstruct the remaining selected Fisher 1922 estimation arguments so that each estimate and theorem has explicit model, sampling and regularity scope. (i) The ML large-sample probable-error/efficiency argument (pp.328-332, including the p.332 multiparameter Hessian rule), stated as a theorem with exact existence, identification, localization, remainder and limit conditions and a written proof. (ii) A correct general form of the sec.7 sufficiency argument (pp.330-331), such as a factorization criterion with the conditions under which the maximizer is a function of a sufficient statistic. (iii) Sec.8 Pearson Type III method-of-moments efficiency, individually and jointly (from p.332). (iv) Location/scaling of frequency curves and intrinsic accuracy, plus the Pearson-curve regimes including Type VII and near-normal moment efficiency (p.353). (v) The Poisson-series and dilution-method arguments. (vi) For grouped data: the fixed-phase periodic-remainder bound for information, existence and a limit theorem for the grouped MLE, and goodness-of-fit calibration of D/Q.

MP-0: The following are owed and absent. (a) A uniform quantitative bound on the fixed-phase periodic remainder of the grouped-normal information; fisher-grouping-and-moments.tex lines 350-356 says it is not established. (b) Existence and limit (consistency/asymptotic normality) of grouped MLEs, with identification after grouping (lines 358-362). (c) Goodness-of-fit calibration: the sampling distribution, degrees-of-freedom adjustment and calibration of D and Q (lines 217-219). (d) Fisher's sec.8 Pearson Type III method-of-moments efficiency, individually and jointly (from p.332). (e) Location and scaling of frequency curves / intrinsic accuracy. (f) The Pearson-curve regime and near-normal moment efficiency arguments (e.g. Type VII, p.353). (g) The Poisson-series and dilution-method arguments.
